VII. ALTERNATIVES TO THE PROPOSED ACTION
The major alternatives to the proposed project are as follows (see Matrix at beginning of Part V for a summary of relationship).
1. No Public Action
Obviously, no public action in the project area would prevent the occurance of the negative impacts, heretofore mentioned, that would be likely if the proposed project is approved. It is also obvious that no public action would deprive the area of the positive aspects of the proposed project. The disadvantages of increased air pollution, noise pollution, water pollution, relocation discomforts, loss of tax base, and the danger of possible future damage due to the unprotected 100 year flood plain, must be weighed against the advantages of: financial aid to the flood victims in the form of relocation assistance, financial aid to the City to repair storm damaged public facilities ( and for the further improvement of same), the arrestment fo brighting influences in the area, funds for the carrying out of flood plain conservation, etc.
The conclusion is that the relative advantages outweigh the relative disadvantage, environmentally, by such a large margin that the project should be approved based on "trade off" of advantages versus disadvantages. Additionally, the extent to which totally adverse, negative, or irreversible ecological or environmental factors were found to be present, would not override the "trade off" premise given above.
2. More Flood Control
A number of proposals have been considered, by the various parties involved, to prevent or reduce the likelihood of future flooding in the project area. Under consideration, and included in the aforementioned environmental impact statement prepared by the U. S. Army Corps of Engineers (covering a proposed wall and levee system to protect South Harrisburg from flooding of the Susquehanna River and Paxta Creek), is a list of the major methods that could be employed to prevent future flooding along the Susquehanna River in the area of the project. They are in part:
a. Wall or levee system along full length of Front Street.
b. Upstream impoundments on the Susquehanna River.
c. Channel improvements to improve river flow past Harristurg.
d. River obstruction removal.
e. Diversion of the Susquehanna River at some point north of the City.
f. Construction of floodways alongside the river.
